vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-34040
vulnerability.description: moby/dockerd authorization-plugin (AuthZ) bypass via oversized request body; daemon-side. Fixed in github.com/moby/moby 29.3.1.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-34040 is an authorization-plugin (AuthZ) bypass in the moby/dockerd DAEMON. build-godynamic ships only the docker-compose CLIENT binary (built from github.com/docker/compose). It links client-side packages of github.com/docker/docker@28.5.2 -- dragged in transitively via github.com/docker/buildx -- but NOT the daemon AuthZ request-handling code, which is not present in the binary's call graph and never executes. No in-place fix exists: the 29.3.1 fix lives only on the github.com/moby/moby module path, while the legacy github.com/docker/docker module is frozen at 28.5.2 and buildx still pins it (even on master). Remediation is upstream-gated and tracked in docs/upstream-cve-backlog.md; drop this statement and bump DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION once buildx drops github.com/docker/docker.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2025-47273
vulnerability.description: setuptools path traversal in PackageIndex.download (setuptools/package_index.py), the deprecated easy_install download path, leading to arbitrary file write. Affects <78.1.1; fixed in setuptools 78.1.1.

statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable file is not in the image. CVE-2025-47273 lives in setuptools/package_index.py (PackageIndex.download). pip does NOT vendor that module: pip/_vendor/ contains pkg_resources -- a separate top-level package that ships in the setuptools distribution -- but there is no pip/_vendor/setuptools/ directory at all. Verified directly by creating a clean venv and listing pip/_vendor/: the entries are cachecontrol, certifi, chardet, colorama, distlib, distro, idna, msgpack, packaging, pkg_resources, platformdirs, pygments, pyparsing, pyproject_hooks, requests, resolvelib, rich, six, tenacity, tomli, truststore, typing_extensions, urllib3, webencodings -- setuptools is absent. The finding is therefore an artifact of pip's vendor.txt metadata being read into its SBOM, not of vulnerable code being present. This is an absence claim, not a reachability argument: there is no code path to reach because the file does not exist in the image. SOURCE: all three findings resolve to a single location in the image -- /az/venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json, the SBOM pip ships describing its OWN vendored dependencies. They are not azure-cli dependencies and not top-level site-packages installs. NO UPSTREAM FIX EXISTS: pip pins its vendored set in pip/_vendor/vendor.txt, and every release from 26.0.1 through 26.2.1 (current at time of writing) still pins setuptools==70.3.0 and msgpack==1.1.2. Upgrading pip therefore does not clear these. Neither does upgrading azure-cli's own dependencies: a top-level `msgpack>=1.2.1` installs alongside, leaving pip/_vendor/msgpack untouched (azure-cli 2.87.0 does resolve cleanly against msgpack 1.2.1 -- verified -- but that is not the reported package). The only in-image lever would be deleting pip from /az/venv, which breaks `az extension add` (it shells out to pip) and is a runtime-contract change, not upkeep. DROP TRIGGER: a pip release that refreshes pip/_vendor/vendor.txt to setuptools>=78.1.1 and msgpack>=1.2.1; then rebuild and delete these statements. Tracked in docs/upstream-cve-backlog.md.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-57585
vulnerability.description: msgpack out-of-bounds read / crash on Unpacker reuse after a caught error, potentially a denial of service. Affects <1.2.1; fixed in msgpack 1.2.1. Same defect as GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964.

statements.impact_statement: Unlike the setuptools statement above, pip/_vendor/msgpack/ IS present in the image, so this is a reachability argument and is scoped narrowly. pip's sole use of vendored msgpack is inside pip/_vendor/cachecontrol, which serializes and deserializes pip's OWN local HTTP cache. The vulnerable path requires feeding crafted MessagePack bytes to an Unpacker that is reused after a caught error; in this image the only bytes reaching that Unpacker are cache entries pip itself wrote to its own cache directory. An adversary able to write that cache already has filesystem write access inside the container, at which point a msgpack DoS is not the marginal risk. The impact is availability-only (a crash of pip), with no confidentiality or integrity component, and pip runs only during image build and explicit `az extension add` invocations -- it is not a network-facing service in this image. buildenv does not run pip against untrusted registries or attacker-supplied caches. SOURCE: all three findings resolve to a single location in the image -- /az/venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json, the SBOM pip ships describing its OWN vendored dependencies. They are not azure-cli dependencies and not top-level site-packages installs. NO UPSTREAM FIX EXISTS: pip pins its vendored set in pip/_vendor/vendor.txt, and every release from 26.0.1 through 26.2.1 (current at time of writing) still pins setuptools==70.3.0 and msgpack==1.1.2. Upgrading pip therefore does not clear these. Neither does upgrading azure-cli's own dependencies: a top-level `msgpack>=1.2.1` installs alongside, leaving pip/_vendor/msgpack untouched (azure-cli 2.87.0 does resolve cleanly against msgpack 1.2.1 -- verified -- but that is not the reported package). The only in-image lever would be deleting pip from /az/venv, which breaks `az extension add` (it shells out to pip) and is a runtime-contract change, not upkeep. DROP TRIGGER: a pip release that refreshes pip/_vendor/vendor.txt to setuptools>=78.1.1 and msgpack>=1.2.1; then rebuild and delete these statements. Tracked in docs/upstream-cve-backlog.md.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-97689
vulnerability.description: urllib3 allocation of resources without limits / throttling: a malicious or misbehaving server response can drive unbounded resource consumption in the client, a denial of service (availability-only). Affects >=1.10.3,<2.8.0; fixed in urllib3 2.8.0.

statements.impact_statement: This is the SAME class as the pip-vendored setuptools (CVE-2025-47273) and msgpack (CVE-2026-57585 / GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964) statements above, and the SAME root location. SOURCE: the finding resolves to pip's OWN vendored urllib3 -- /az/venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pip/_vendor/urllib3, reported via /az/venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json (the SBOM pip ships describing its vendored dependencies). It is NOT the azure-cli dependency: the top-level urllib3 that azure-cli 2.87.0 installs into /az/venv is already 2.8.0 (the fixed version -- azure-cli does not pin urllib3, so a fresh build resolves it to 2.8.0; verified in the image at /az/venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/urllib3-2.8.0.dist-info). The ONLY vulnerable copy is pip's internal vendored one. REACHABILITY: pip's vendored urllib3 (via pip/_vendor/requests) is used solely by pip itself to fetch packages from the configured package index over HTTPS -- at image-build time and on explicit `az extension add`. CVE-2026-97689 is an availability-only DoS that triggers when the server pip talks to returns a crafted/unbounded response; pip connects only to the trusted configured index (PyPI), whose responses an adversary does not control. There is no network-facing service in this image that feeds attacker-controlled HTTP responses to pip's vendored urllib3, so the vulnerable path is not reachable with adversary-controlled input. NO UPSTREAM FIX EXISTS: pip pins its vendored set in pip/_vendor/vendor.txt, and the current release 26.2.1 (the latest at time of writing -- verified: `import pip._vendor.urllib3; urllib3.__version__` == 2.7.0) still vendors urllib3 2.7.0. Upgrading pip does not clear it. The only in-image lever would be deleting pip from /az/venv, which breaks `az extension add` (it shells out to pip) and is a runtime-contract change, not upkeep. DROP TRIGGER: a pip release that refreshes pip/_vendor/vendor.txt to urllib3>=2.8.0; then rebuild and delete this statement (together with CVE-2026-97687). Tracked in docs/upstream-cve-backlog.md.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-97687
vulnerability.description: urllib3 improper certificate validation when using an HTTPS proxy: target-specific TLS identity / certificate assertions are applied to the proxy connection, so a malicious HTTPS proxy can be accepted against the target's cert expectations. Affects >=1.26.0,<2.8.0; fixed in urllib3 2.8.0.

statements.impact_statement: Same SOURCE and same pip-vendored root as CVE-2026-97689 (read that statement for the full source/upstream analysis): the finding is pip's OWN vendored urllib3 at /az/venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pip/_vendor/urllib3 (reported via pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json), NOT the azure-cli dependency -- the top-level urllib3 azure-cli installs is already the fixed 2.8.0. REACHABILITY for THIS CVE: CVE-2026-97687 misapplies target-specific TLS identity/credentials to an HTTPS PROXY connection, so it can only be triggered when the client is configured to reach the index through an attacker-controlled HTTPS proxy. pip in this image is configured with no HTTPS proxy, and the proxy configuration (HTTPS_PROXY / pip's --proxy) is operator-controlled, not adversary-controlled; a remote attacker cannot inject a malicious proxy into pip's build-time index fetches. pip's vendored urllib3 is exercised only for pip's own package-index traffic (image build / explicit `az extension add`), never as a network-facing service handling attacker-routed connections, so the vulnerable proxy-cert-validation path is not reachable with adversary-controlled input. NO UPSTREAM FIX EXISTS: pip 26.2.1 (latest) still vendors urllib3 2.7.0; upgrading pip does not clear it, and deleting pip from /az/venv breaks `az extension add`. DROP TRIGGER: a pip release that refreshes pip/_vendor/vendor.txt to urllib3>=2.8.0; then rebuild and delete this statement (together with CVE-2026-97689). Tracked in docs/upstream-cve-backlog.md.
